task: T7.5 - structured logs and env-optional Sentry

mutants.name: M-log-level-channel
mutants.kills: an error must land on the error channel, not merely somewhere

mutants.name: M-log-one-line
mutants.kills: one entry is one line - a pretty-printed entry breaks every aggregator

mutants.name: M-log-clock-injection
mutants.kills: the timestamp comes from the injected clock, so tests assert a literal

mutants.name: M-log-sink-injection
mutants.kills: an injected sink replaces the console rather than being ignored

mutants.name: M-log-correlation-key
mutants.anchor: return createLogger({ key: "request_id", value: requestId }, options, {});
mutants.replacement: return createLogger({ key: "job_id", value: requestId }, options, {});
mutants.kills: a request logger emits request_id, not job_id

mutants.name: M-log-reserved-keys
mutants.kills: a caller-supplied field cannot relabel level/time/msg/request_id

mutants.name: M-log-correlation-missing-off
mutants.kills: a blank correlation id is flagged, so untraceable lines are greppable

mutants.name: M-log-correlation-missing-always
mutants.kills: the flag is not stamped on a line that HAS an id

mutants.name: M-log-with-bound-fields
mutants.kills: fields bound by with() appear on every later entry

mutants.name: M-log-error-serialize
mutants.kills: THE TRAP - an Error handed straight to JSON.stringify becomes {}

mutants.name: M-log-error-stack
mutants.kills: the stack survives - 'which line threw' is the whole point

mutants.name: M-log-error-cause
mutants.kills: the cause chain survives - the real fault is usually at the bottom

mutants.name: M-log-error-code
mutants.kills: a driver error code (23505, 42501) survives

mutants.name: M-log-error-cross-realm
mutants.kills: an Error from another realm is still serialized, not silently emptied

mutants.name: M-log-redact-keys-off
mutants.kills: every secret-shaped key is redacted

mutants.name: M-log-redact-keys-everything
mutants.kills: route/user_id/receipt_id are NOT redacted - over-redaction is also a defect

mutants.name: M-log-redact-at-emit
mutants.anchor: entry[key] = isSensitiveKey(key) ? REDACTED : walk(value, 1, new WeakSet<object>());
mutants.kills: a top-level secret field is redacted, including one bound by with()

mutants.name: M-log-redact-nested
mutants.anchor: result[key] = isSensitiveKey(key) ? REDACTED : walk(entry, depth + 1, seen);
mutants.kills: redaction reaches inside nested objects and arrays, not just the top

mutants.name: M-log-redact-jwt
mutants.kills: a JWT is redacted by shape even under an innocent key

mutants.name: M-log-redact-bearer
mutants.kills: a bearer credential is redacted by shape even under an innocent key

mutants.name: M-log-circular
mutants.kills: a cycle is named, not walked

mutants.name: M-log-circular-siblings
mutants.kills: a shared sibling object is printed twice, not misreported as a cycle

mutants.name: M-log-depth-cap
mutants.kills: the walk stops at a depth cap

mutants.name: M-log-array-cap
mutants.kills: a capped array says how many entries it dropped

mutants.name: M-log-string-cap
mutants.kills: a huge string is truncated rather than becoming the log line

mutants.name: M-log-bigint
mutants.kills: a bigint does not make JSON.stringify throw the entry away

mutants.name: M-log-nonfinite
mutants.kills: NaN/Infinity are named, not silently emitted as null

mutants.name: M-log-headers
mutants.replacement: if (false && typeof Headers !== "undefined" && object instanceof Headers) {

mutants.name: M-log-map
mutants.kills: a Map does not stringify to {}

mutants.name: M-log-set
mutants.kills: a Set does not stringify to {}

mutants.name: M-log-date
mutants.kills: a Date renders as an ISO string

mutants.name: M-log-invalid-date
mutants.kills: an invalid Date is named rather than throwing the entry away

mutants.name: M-log-regexp
mutants.kills: a RegExp does not stringify to {}

mutants.anchor:
} catch {

mutants.name: M-log-release
mutants.kills: 'on which deploy' - the commit sha is stamped on the line

mutants.name: M-log-release-blank
mutants.kills: off-platform the key is omitted, not emitted as an empty string

mutants.name: M-handler-drop-request-id
mutants.kills: THE BRIEF'S NAMED MUTANT - drop the id from the adopted call site

mutants.name: M-handler-drop-route
mutants.kills: the line names the route that threw

mutants.name: M-handler-drop-user
mutants.kills: 'for which user' - a signed-in caller is named, not flattened to anonymous

mutants.name: M-handler-anonymous-fallback
mutants.kills: the user_id key is always present, never null - a sometimes-absent field is unfilterable

mutants.name: M-handler-user-hoist
mutants.kills: the hoisted userId is actually assigned from the resolved session

mutants.name: M-handler-drop-error
mutants.kills: 'which line threw' - the throw itself reaches the line, name/message/stack

mutants.name: M-handler-drop-status
mutants.kills: the line reports the status the caller actually received

mutants.replacement: if (isApiError(error)) { log().error("unhandled error", { err: error, status: 500 });

mutants.replacement: log().error("idempotency gate unavailable, failing closed", { status: 503 });

mutants.name: M-handler-request-id-delegates
mutants.kills: the handler passes the INBOUND header to the shared screen, not nothing

mutants.name: M-ocr-drop-job-id
mutants.kills: THE BRIEF'S NAMED MUTANT - drop the id from the adopted call site (ocr.process)

mutants.name: M-ocr-drop-receipt-id
mutants.kills: the line names the receipt - the id a support ticket actually arrives with

mutants.name: M-ocr-drop-worker
mutants.kills: the line names which worker wrote it

mutants.name: M-ocr-drop-throw
mutants.kills: the pipeline's own throw reaches the line, not just the fact that one happened

mutants.name: M-ocr-drop-read-error
mutants.anchor: log.error("could not read the receipt outcome", { err: error, outcome: "unreadable" });
mutants.replacement: log.error("could not read the receipt outcome", { outcome: "unreadable" });
mutants.kills: the failed status read says what the database actually answered

mutants.name: M-ocr-gone-not-logged
mutants.kills: a signed job for a receipt that does not exist is still reported

mutants.name: M-ocr-terminal-status-field
mutants.anchor: log.info("terminal outcome; acking", { status: data.status, outcome: "terminal" });
mutants.kills: the status is a FIELD, not a word inside a sentence a regex has to reach into

mutants.name: M-email-drop-job-id
mutants.kills: THE BRIEF'S NAMED MUTANT - drop the id from the adopted call site (notify.email)

mutants.name: M-email-batch-read-error
mutants.replacement: log.error("could not read the batch", { requested: payload.notification_ids.length });
mutants.kills: the unreadable batch says what the database answered

mutants.name: M-email-summary-counts
mutants.kills: the batch counts are aggregatable fields, not numbers inside a sentence

mutants.replacement: const suppression = await suppressionReason(deps.supabase, row.user_id, row.kind, jobLogger(""));

mutants.name: M-email-preferences-error
mutants.anchor: log.error("could not read preferences; failing closed", { err: error, user_id: userId });
mutants.replacement: log.error("could not read preferences; failing closed", { user_id: userId });
mutants.kills: the fail-closed suppression says why the read failed

mutants.name: M-email-address-leak
mutants.kills: the recipient's address never reaches a log line

mutants.name: M-log-request-id-screen
mutants.kills: the ONE screen - a malformed inbound id is discarded everywhere, not echoed

mutants.name: M-log-request-id-no-propagate
mutants.kills: the ONE screen - a well-formed inbound id propagates everywhere

mutants.name: M-log-request-id-fallback
mutants.kills: a runtime with no Web Crypto still mints an id its own screen accepts

mutants.name: M-sentry-dsn-malformed
mutants.kills: a blank, whitespace or typo'd DSN reads as ABSENT, never handed to Sentry.init

mutants.name: M-sentry-client-dsn-fallback
mutants.kills: the browser reads only NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN - the other is unreachable there

mutants.name: M-sentry-pii
mutants.kills: Sentry never decides for itself what counts as personal data here

mutants.name: M-sentry-traces-default
mutants.kills: tracing is off by default and a typo'd rate cannot become a 100% bill

mutants.name: M-sentry-release
mutants.kills: the release is set at RUNTIME, since no build plugin will inject one

mutants.name: M-sentry-beforesend
mutants.kills: events are scrubbed on the way out, not merely scrubbable

mutants.name: M-sentry-beforesend-transaction
mutants.kills: transactions are scrubbed too - they carry the same request object

mutants.name: M-sentry-header-allowlist
mutants.kills: the body, query string and cookies are DROPPED, not merely joined by an allowlist

mutants.name: M-sentry-header-denylist
mutants.kills: headers are ALLOWlisted - authorization, cookie and x-forwarded-for never forward

mutants.name: M-sentry-user-pii
mutants.kills: the user's email, username and IP never reach Sentry; the id does

mutants.name: M-sentry-redact-extra
mutants.kills: src/lib/log.ts's own redaction applies to anything forwarded - one scrubber, not two

mutants.name: M-sentry-no-mutate
mutants.kills: scrubbing does not mutate the caller's event

mutants.name: M-instr-noise-without-dsn
mutants.kills: the disabled path writes NOTHING to any console channel
